That helper compares the stored point value and updates display/text state, supporting the training-point-change and notification wording. No indexed caller for this target was found.

Confirmed. The routine initializes the caller output to -1, exits if either the global context entry or its +0x78 object pointer is absent, and only then calls format_player_attribute_value_line with mode 1. It stores a later result into the caller output only when that result is at most 9. This supports the guarded formatting name without assigning an attribute meaning. No indexed callers were found.

The body queries attribute-context selector 4 and uses the returned status byte to validate and bucket the dispatched context value. It returns -2 when that selector result is outside 3..9, otherwise returns a bucket from 0..3 based on status-derived thresholds. The proposal wording “context_status_4” could imply status equals 4; the body uses selector 4 and accepts several status values. The indexed caller routes event 0x29b here and consumes the returned classification, so I corrected the name to make the selector relationship explicit.
